newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Normandy questions central bank gold sale.
newsitem.headline: Normandy questions central bank gold sale.

text.p: The head of Australia's biggest gold producer said on Thursday the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to sell 167 tonnes of gold brought into question the wisdom of having an independent central bank.
"It calls into question whether independence is such a good thing," Normandy Mining Ltd chairman Robert de Crespigny told a media briefing.
De Crespigny said he would be interested to know the thinking behind the decision to sell, which contributed to the gold price falling to 12 year lows when it was announced last week.
"The Reserve Bank clearly thought that earning A$80 million worth of interest was more important than an adverse balance of payments and more unemployment," he said.
The Reserve Bank, which reduced its gold holdings to 80 tonnes from 247 tonnes, said it would invest the proceeds from the sale in foreign currency assets.
However, de Crespigny said the decision also showed the gold industry needed more political clout and had not sold its story strongly enough in Canberra.
He said he spoke on Wednesday night with Treasurer Peter Costello, who he described as a big supporter of the industry.
De Crespigny, who acknowledged he had been one of many people who had supported central bank independence, also said it was time to end the debate over the sales which was no longer constructive.
"The decision has been made and the ounces have been sold," he said.
